title: Which Wounded-but-Healed Bible Figure Are You?
subtitle: Six people who limped out the other side, and what got them there.

questions.text: What kind of wound shaped your story most?

options.text: People I trusted turned on me.
Loss after loss left me bitter and empty.
A long, draining suffering nobody could fix.
Something happened to me as a child that I never chose.

questions.text: When you were at your lowest, what did it sound like inside?

options.text: "Even the people who should love me threw me away."
"Don't even call me by my name anymore. Call me bitter."
"I've tried everything and nothing's changed."
"There's no place at the table for someone like me."

questions.text: Be honest about a harder part of your past:

options.text: I was on the wrong side of things and caused real harm.
I got used and then cast out when I was no longer wanted.
I was betrayed by family and left for dead, basically.
I bled out years on a problem that just kept taking.

questions.text: How did your healing actually start?

options.text: By choosing to forgive the people who hurt me.
By letting God rename a season I thought was only loss.
By reaching out in desperation for one more chance.
By being met in the desert when I had nothing left.

questions.text: What do you now believe about your worst chapter?

options.text: What others meant for evil, God meant for good.
The empty season wasn't the end of my story.
My faith reached Him, and He didn't pull away.
If grace can reach me, it can reach anyone.

questions.text: Where do you see God most clearly now?

options.text: Turning betrayal into the very thing that saved people.
Filling back what loss had emptied.
Calling me "daughter" when I expected to be scolded.
Carrying me to a table and seating me as family.

questions.text: What's the gift your wound left behind?

options.text: I can hold power without using it to get even.
I'm tender now with other people in their grief.
I'll keep reaching for Jesus no matter how it looks.
I tell everyone what mercy did for me.

questions.text: Which line makes your eyes sting?

options.text: "You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good."
"The God who sees me found me in the wilderness."
"Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace."
"You will always have a seat at my table."

questions.text: What's the hope you'd hand to someone still bleeding?

options.text: "The pit isn't the end. There's a purpose ahead."
"Bitter isn't your final name."
"He's not too holy to be touched by your mess."
"You were seen the whole time, even out there alone."

joseph.name: Joseph (Betrayed, Then Restored)
joseph.description: You know what it is to be betrayed by the people who were supposed to protect you. And somehow you came out the other side without becoming bitter. You can hold influence now without using it to settle old scores. What others meant for harm, God has been quietly weaving into rescue. That's a rare kind of healing.

scripture.text: And as for you, ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

naomi.name: Naomi (Bitter, Then Renamed)
naomi.description: You've known loss heavy enough that you once would have told people to call you by a different name, a bitter one. But the empty season wasn't your ending. God has a way of filling back what grief hollowed out, and your tenderness toward other hurting people is proof the bitterness didn't win.

scripture.text: And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be Jehovah, who hath not left thee this day without a near kinsman; and let his name be famous in Israel.

bleeding-woman.name: The Bleeding Woman (Suffering, Then Touched)
bleeding-woman.description: You've spent years on a suffering that drained everything and changed nothing. But you kept reaching. When you finally touched the edge of His cloak, He didn't recoil or scold you. He called you daughter and sent you off in peace. Your healing was always more than physical, and so is His tenderness toward you.

scripture.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

mephibosheth.name: Mephibosheth (Crippled, Then Seated at the Table)
mephibosheth.description: Something happened to you that you never chose, and it left you sure you'd been written off. Then a King sought you out, not to punish you, but to show you kindness. He gave you a permanent seat at His own table and called you family. Where you were wounded, you've been welcomed home.

scripture.text: And David said unto him, Fear not; for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

paul.name: Paul (The Persecutor Made Apostle)
paul.description: You carry a past you're not proud of, a chapter where you caused real harm. But grace reached all the way down and turned you completely around. Now your story is the loudest argument you have that no one is too far gone. You don't hide the before. You let it show how big the mercy was.

scripture.text: Faithful is the saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief:

hagar.name: Hagar (Cast Out, Seen by God)
hagar.description: You've been used and then sent away, left in a wilderness with no map and no people. But out there, where you were certain no one was watching, God met you and called you by name. You learned the truth that carries you still: He is the God who sees. You were never as alone as it felt.

scripture.text: And she called the name of Jehovah that spake unto her, Thou art a God that seeth: for she said, Have I even here looked after him that seeth me?
